records.source: וַיְהִ֞י מִקֵּ֣ץ׀עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּנָ֧ה שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of twenty years which built Solomon the house of Yahweh and his house,
pieces: At the end of the twenty years it took Solomon to build {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s house and his own palace,

L.1: And it happened at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and his own house,

R.1: It took Solomon twenty years to build {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple and his own palace.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 9:10, with "his own house" for "the two houses, the house of the LORD and the house of the king"
decisions.reason: Chapter 8 retells 1 Kings 9:10-28. This verse matches 1 Kings 9:10 except that it says "his own house" where Kings names "the two houses" and calls the second "the house of the king". Both mean the temple and the royal palace.

decisions.choice: twenty years: seven for the temple and thirteen for the palace
decisions.reason: The temple took seven years (1 Kings 6:38) and the palace thirteen (1 Kings 7:1), so the whole building program lasted twenty years. Chronicles tells only of the temple (chapters 3-7) and assumes the palace (2:11; 7:11).

decisions.choice: a time clause that runs on into verse 2
decisions.reason: The sentence begins here and reaches its main statement in verse 2, "Solomon rebuilt them".

decisions.choice: It took Solomon twenty years ...
decisions.reason: Readable makes the time clause a sentence of its own, as in 1 Kings 9:10, and starts verse 2 with "Then".

records.heading: Solomon's building and forced labor

records.source: וְהֶעָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֤ן חוּרָם֙ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה בָּנָ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֹתָ֑ם וַיּ֥וֹשֶׁב שָׁ֖ם אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: and the cities which had given Huram to Solomon, built Solomon them and settled there [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him and settled {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in them.

L.2: the cities that Huram had given to Solomon, Solomon built them, and settled the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel there.

R.2: Then Solomon rebuilt the towns that Huram had given him, and he had {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} settle there.

decisions.choice: the cities Huram had given to Solomon; 1 Kings 9:11-13 has Solomon giving Hiram twenty cities
alternatives: Solomon rebuilt the cities he had given to Huram (an emendation to match 1 Kings)
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 9:11-13 Solomon gives Hiram twenty towns in Galilee, and Hiram scorns them. Here the towns are ones Huram gave to Solomon, and Solomon rebuilds them and settles Israelites in them. The two accounts may tell different sides of one exchange: the towns Hiram rejected came back to Solomon, who then built them up. Or they may describe a separate gift. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: Huram: Hiram king of Tyre
decisions.reason: Chronicles spells the king's name Huram (2:2, 10-11); 1 Kings spells it Hiram. It is the same man, Solomon's ally who supplied the timber for the temple.

decisions.choice: built: rebuilt and strengthened
decisions.reason: "Build" is used for rebuilding a town and for fortifying one, as in 1 Kings 9:17. Since the towns already stood, rebuilt is meant.

decisions.choice: towns; rebuilt
decisions.reason: "Towns" suits places of this size, as in 1 Kings 9:11, and "rebuilt" gives the sense of "built" here. Balanced and Readable say "him" for the repeated name Solomon.

records.source: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ חֲמָ֣ת צוֹבָ֔ה וַיֶּחֱזַ֖ק עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And went Solomon [to] Hamath-zobah and prevailed over it.
pieces: Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and seized it.

L.3: And Solomon went [to] Hamath-zobah and prevailed over it.

R.3: Solomon marched to Hamath-zobah and captured it.

decisions.choice: Hamath-zobah: not in 1 Kings 9
decisions.reason: This verse has no parallel in 1 Kings. It is the only military campaign of Solomon's that the Bible records. It explains how Solomon came to build store cities "in Hamath" (verse 4).

decisions.choice: Hamath-zobah: Hamath, in or near the region of Zobah, north of Israel
decisions.reason: Hamath was a kingdom on the Orontes River in Syria, whose king made peace with David (1 Chronicles 18:9-10). Zobah was the Aramean kingdom David defeated (1 Chronicles 18:3). The joined name probably points to the land of Hamath bordering Zobah; it may also be one town called by both names.

decisions.choice: prevailed over it: took control of it
decisions.reason: The verb means "be strong"; with "over" it means to overpower or seize a place.

decisions.choice: marched to
decisions.reason: Readable says "marched" because the verb "went" here means going with an army, as "captured" shows.

records.source: וַיִּ֥בֶן אֶת־תַּדְמֹ֖ר בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וְאֵת֙ כָּל־עָרֵ֣י הַֽמִּסְכְּנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה בַּחֲמָֽת׃
records.gloss: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the cities of the stores which he built in Hamath.
pieces: He built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the store cities that he built in Hamath.

L.4: And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the cities of storage that he built in Hamath.

R.4: He built Tadmor in the desert, and all the towns in the region of Hamath where he stored supplies.

decisions.choice: Tadmor in the wilderness; 1 Kings 9:18 has Tamar in the wilderness, in the land
decisions.reason: The written text of 1 Kings 9:18 spells Tamar, a town on the southern edge of the land, though it is traditionally read aloud as Tadmor. Chronicles has Tadmor in its written text and drops "in the land". It also places the store cities "in Hamath", where 1 Kings 9:19 has store cities "that belonged to Solomon" (repeated here in verse 6).

decisions.choice: Tadmor: an oasis in the Syrian desert, later called Palmyra
decisions.reason: Tadmor lay in the desert northeast of Hamath, on the caravan road between Syria and the Euphrates. Building there fits the move into Hamath in verse 3.

decisions.choice: cities of storage: towns where grain and supplies were stored
decisions.reason: Royal store cities held food and supplies for the army and the court, like those Israel built for Pharaoh (Exodus 1:11).

decisions.choice: desert; towns ... where he stored supplies
decisions.reason: Readable says "desert" for wilderness and explains store cities, as in 1 Kings 9:18-19.

records.source: וַיִּ֜בֶן אֶת־בֵּ֤ית חוֹרוֹן֙ הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן וְאֶת־בֵּ֥ית חוֹר֖וֹן הַתַּחְתּ֑וֹן עָרֵ֣י מָצ֔וֹר חוֹמ֖וֹת דְּלָתַ֥יִם וּבְרִֽיחַ׃
records.gloss: And he built Beth-horon the upper and Beth-horon the lower, cities of fortification, walls, doors and bar,
pieces: He also built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon as fortified towns, with walls, gates and bars,

L.5: And he built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities [with] walls, doors and bars,

R.5: He built up the towns of Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon and made them strong. He gave them walls, and gates with bars to lock them.

decisions.choice: Upper and Lower Beth-horon; 1 Kings 9:17 names only Lower Beth-horon
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:17 lists Gezer and Lower Beth-horon. Chronicles does not name Gezer, adds Upper Beth-horon, and describes the towns' walls and gates.

decisions.choice: Beth-horon: two towns guarding the pass up from the coastal plain
decisions.reason: Upper and Lower Beth-horon stood on the main road from the coast to the hill country north of Jerusalem (Joshua 10:10-11; 16:3, 5).

decisions.choice: doors and bar: the two leaves of a city gate and the beam that locked them
decisions.reason: A city gate had two doors that were shut and held by a bar laid across them (Deuteronomy 3:5).

decisions.choice: the list runs on into verse 6
decisions.reason: Verse 6 continues the list of what Solomon built, still governed by "he built".

decisions.choice: gates and bars (Balanced); gates with bars to lock them (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Doors" of a city are its gates, so Balanced and Readable say "gates", and Readable says what the bars were for.

records.source: וְאֶֽת־בַּעֲלָ֗ת וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־עָרֵ֤י הַֽמִּסְכְּנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָי֣וּ לִשְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וְאֵת֙ כָּל־עָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְאֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַפָּרָשִׁ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת׀כָּל־חֵ֣שֶׁק שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשַׁק֙ לִבְנ֤וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּבַלְּבָנ֔וֹן וּבְכֹ֖ל אֶ֥רֶץ מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: and Baalath and all the cities of the stores which belonged to Solomon, and all the cities of the chariotry and the cities of the horsemen, and all the desire of Solomon which he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all [the] land of his dominion.
pieces: and Baalath, all the store cities that Solomon had, all the towns for his chariots and for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout all the land he ruled.

L.6: and Baalath, and all the cities of storage that belonged to Solomon, and all the cities of the chariots and the cities of the horsemen, and all the desire of Solomon that he desired to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.

R.6: He also built Baalath, all the towns where he stored supplies, and all the towns for his chariots and his horsemen. He built whatever he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and everywhere in the land he ruled.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 9:18-19, with "all" added before the chariot cities and before Solomon's desire
decisions.reason: The verse follows 1 Kings 9:18-19 closely. Tamar has moved to verse 4 as Tadmor, and "all" is added twice. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Baalath: a town in the territory of Dan
decisions.reason: Baalath is listed among Dan's towns (Joshua 19:44), not far from Beth-horon.

decisions.choice: horsemen: the men who rode or drove the horses, or the horses themselves
decisions.reason: The word can mean either. Solomon's chariots and horses are counted in 1:14.

decisions.choice: the desire of Solomon that he desired: whatever he set his heart on
decisions.reason: The noun and verb repeat one root: these were the projects Solomon wanted for himself (compare 7:11).

decisions.choice: whatever Solomon desired to build; the land he ruled
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 9:19, Balanced and Readable turn "the desire ... that he desired" into a plain clause, and "the land of his dominion" into "the land he ruled".

records.source: כָּל־הָ֠עָם הַנּוֹתָ֨ר מִן־הַחִתִּ֜י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֤י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹ֥א מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: All the people who remained of the Hittite[s] and the Amorite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s], who not of Israel [were] they,
pieces: As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, who were not part of Israel,

L.7: All the people who were left of the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, who [were] not of Israel,

R.7: Some of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites were still left in the land. These people were not part of Israel.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 9:20, with the Hittites named before the Amorites and "not of Israel" for "not of the sons of Israel"
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 9:20 with two small changes: the first two peoples change places, and "Israel" stands for "the sons of Israel". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites: the peoples of Canaan before Israel
decisions.reason: These names belong to the standard list of the land's earlier inhabitants (Exodus 3:8; Deuteronomy 7:1; Joshua 9:1).

decisions.choice: all the people who were left: placed first and taken up again in verse 8
decisions.reason: The verse names the group, and verse 8 continues "from their descendants ... Solomon raised forced labor". The sentence ends there.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable states who these peoples were in sentences of their own before verse 8 says what Solomon did with them, as in 1 Kings 9:20.

records.source: מִן־בְּנֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר נוֹתְר֤וּ אַחֲרֵיהֶם֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־כִלּ֖וּם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעֲלֵ֤ם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔ס עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: of their sons who remained after them in the land whom not had destroyed them [the] sons of Israel, and raised them Solomon for forced labor until the day this.
pieces: from their descendants who were still left in the land, whom the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not destroyed, Solomon conscripted forced labor, to this day.

L.8: of their {{gender:children|sons}} who were left after them in the land, whom the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel had not destroyed, Solomon raised them for forced labor, to this day.

R.8: They were the descendants of the peoples the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} had not destroyed. Solomon made them do forced labor, as they still do to this day.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 9:21, with "destroyed" for "been able to devote to destruction" and without "as slaves"
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:21 says Israel "had not been able to devote them to destruction" and that Solomon raised them "for forced labor of slaving". Chronicles says simply that Israel "had not destroyed them" and that Solomon raised them "for forced labor". It also begins "from their descendants", that is, the workers were drawn from among them. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: forced labor: workers called up by the king to work without pay
decisions.reason: Kings conscripted men for their building works (1 Kings 5:27-28; 9:15). Verse 9 says that Israelites were not made slaves for this work.

decisions.choice: to this day: the words of the earlier account
decisions.reason: The phrase comes over from 1 Kings 9:21, where it means the time of that writer, while the kingdom of Judah still stood. Chronicles keeps the words of its source, as at 5:9; by its own time, after the exile, no king of Israel ruled to raise forced labor.

decisions.choice: conscripted
decisions.reason: The verb is "raised" or "brought up", used of calling up a workforce, as in 1 Kings 9:21; Balanced says what it means.

records.source: וּמִן־בְּנֵי֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא־נָתַ֧ן שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה לַעֲבָדִ֖ים לִמְלַאכְתּ֑וֹ כִּי־הֵ֜מָּה אַנְשֵׁ֤י מִלְחָמָה֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י שָׁלִישָׁ֔יו וְשָׂרֵ֥י רִכְבּ֖וֹ וּפָרָשָֽׁיו׃פ
records.gloss: But of [the] sons of Israel, whom not made Solomon into slaves for his work, for they [were] men of war and commanders of his officers and commanders of his chariotry and his horsemen.
pieces: But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} for his work. They were his soldiers, the commanders of his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

L.9: But of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel Solomon did not make [any] slaves for his work; for they [were] men of war, and commanders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

R.9: But Solomon did not make any of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} work for him as slaves. Instead, they served as his soldiers and his chief officers, and they commanded his chariots and his horsemen.

decisions.choice: parallel to 1 Kings 9:22, with "for his work" added and a shorter list of ranks
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:22 lists "the men of war, his servants, his commanders, his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen". Chronicles adds "for his work", leaves out "his servants", and has "commanders of his officers" where Kings has "his commanders and his officers".

decisions.choice: whom Solomon did not make slaves: the main statement of the sentence
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins "but of the sons of Israel, whom Solomon did not make slaves", leaving the sentence open; the sense is that he made none of them slaves.

decisions.choice: officers: a rank in the army
decisions.reason: The word comes from "three" and may first have meant the third man in a chariot. It came to name a high-ranking officer (1 Kings 9:22; 2 Kings 9:25).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" is kept at every level, as in 1 Kings 9:22, because the verse is about who was made a slave.

decisions.choice: soldiers; chief officers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Men of war" is plain "soldiers", and Readable says "chief officers" for "commanders of his officers".

records.source: וְאֵ֨לֶּה שָׂרֵ֤י הַנִּצָּבִ֛יםאֲשֶׁר־לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וּמָאתָ֑יִם הָרֹדִ֖ים בָּעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And these [were] [the] chiefs of the officers who [belonged] to the king Solomon, fifty and two hundred, who ruled over the people.
pieces: These were King Solomon's chief officers: 250 of them, who directed the people.

L.10: And these [were] the chiefs of the officers who belonged to King Solomon: 250, who ruled over the people.

R.10: King Solomon had 250 chief officers. They directed the people who did the work.

decisions.choice: 250 chief officers; 1 Kings 9:23 has 550
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:23 counts 550 chief officers "over the work", with 3,300 officials over the workers in 1 Kings 5:30. Chronicles counts 250 here and 3,600 overseers in 2:17. The numbers likely count different ranks; both books give the same total, 3,850 (3,300 and 550; 3,600 and 250). Chronicles also says the officers "belonged to King Solomon" where Kings says they were "over the work for Solomon".

decisions.choice: officers: the word as read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants and the traditional reading spell this word slightly differently. Both forms come from the verb "to stand, be stationed" and name officials stationed over others, like Solomon's district officers (1 Kings 4:5, 7). The sense is not affected.

decisions.choice: ruled over the people: directed the workforce
decisions.reason: The verb is used of masters over workers and need not mean harshness, though it can (Leviticus 25:43). "The people" here are the workers of verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: directed; the people who did the work (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Directed" gives the supervising sense without the overtones of "ruled", as in 1 Kings 9:23. Readable adds "who did the work" to show who "the people" were.

records.source: וְאֶת־בַּת־פַּרְעֹ֗ה הֶעֱלָ֤ה שְׁלֹמֹה֙ מֵעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד לַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּֽנָה־לָ֑הּ כִּ֣י אָמַ֗ר לֹא־תֵשֵׁ֨ב אִשָּׁ֥ה לִי֙ בְּבֵית֙ דָּוִ֣יד מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּי־קֹ֣דֶשׁ הֵ֔מָּה אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽאָ֥ה אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And [the] daughter of Pharaoh brought up Solomon from [the] city of David to the house which he had built for her, for he said, Not shall dwell a wife of mine in [the] house of David king of Israel, for holiness [are] they where has come to them [the] ark of Yahweh.
pieces: Solomon moved Pharaoh's daughter up from the city of David to the house he had built for her. His reason was this: "No wife of mine is to live in the house of David king of Israel, since the places where the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has come are holy."

L.11: And Solomon brought the daughter of Pharaoh up from the city of David to the house that he had built for her, for he said, "A wife of mine shall not live in the house of David king of Israel, for they [are] holy, [the places] to which the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has come."

R.11: Solomon moved Pharaoh's daughter out of the city of David and into the palace he had built for her. He said, "No wife of mine may live in the palace of David, the king of Israel. The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been in those places, so they are holy."

decisions.choice: Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up, and why; 1 Kings 9:24 says only that she went up
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:24 says that Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her house, and that Solomon then built the Millo. Chronicles makes Solomon the one who moved her, gives his reason, and does not mention the Millo. It also has not told of the marriage itself, which 1 Kings 3:1 and 7:8 describe; it assumes the reader knows it.

decisions.choice: the places the ark has come to are holy
decisions.reason: The ark, the sign of the LORD's presence, had been kept in the city of David in the tent David pitched for it (1 Chronicles 15:1; 16:1; 2 Chronicles 5:2). Solomon judged that the places near where it had stood shared its holiness. The text does not say whether the problem was that she was a foreigner, that she was a woman, or simply that a household should not live there; it states only the holiness of the places.

decisions.choice: they: the buildings of David's house and the places around it
decisions.reason: "They" is plural and refers to the places the ark had come to, which include the house of David just named.

decisions.choice: the house of David: David's palace in the old city
decisions.reason: David had built himself a house in the city of David (1 Chronicles 14:1; 15:1), on the lower ridge south of the temple.

decisions.choice: The ark of the LORD has been in those places, so they are holy.
decisions.reason: Readable splits the reason into a separate sentence and puts the cause first.

records.source: אָ֣ז הֶעֱלָ֧ה שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה עֹל֖וֹת לַיהוָ֑ה עַ֚ל מִזְבַּ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הָאוּלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Then offered up Solomon burnt offerings to Yahweh on [the] altar of Yahweh which he had built before the porch,
pieces: Then Solomon presented burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar, which he had built in front of the porch,

L.12: Then Solomon offered up burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that he had built before the porch,

R.12: Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the altar he had built for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in front of the temple porch.

decisions.choice: an expanded form of 1 Kings 9:25
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:25 says briefly that Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings three times a year on the altar he had built, and burned incense. Chronicles has no peace offerings or incense here, and in verses 13-16 adds the daily, Sabbath and new moon offerings, the command of Moses and David's arrangements for priests, Levites and gatekeepers. These have no parallel in Kings.

decisions.choice: the altar before the porch: the bronze altar in the courtyard
decisions.reason: Solomon's bronze altar stood in the courtyard in front of the temple porch (4:1; 6:13; 7:7). Burnt offerings were made there.

decisions.choice: then: once the temple was finished; the sentence runs on into verse 13
decisions.reason: "Then" follows from the completion of the temple. Verse 13 goes on to say how often the offerings were made.

decisions.choice: the altar he had built for the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says "built for the LORD" rather than repeating "the altar of the LORD", and adds "temple" to the porch.

records.heading: Offerings and temple service

records.source: וּבִדְבַר־י֣וֹם בְּי֗וֹם לְהַעֲלוֹת֙ כְּמִצְוַ֣ת מֹשֶׁ֔ה לַשַּׁבָּתוֹת֙ וְלֶ֣חֳדָשִׁ֔ים וְלַמּ֣וֹעֲד֔וֹת שָׁל֥וֹשׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה בְּחַ֧ג הַמַּצּ֛וֹת וּבְחַ֥ג הַשָּׁבֻע֖וֹת וּבְחַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: and by [the] matter of a day in a day to offer up according to [the] commandment of Moses for the sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed times three times in the year, at [the] festival of the unleavened bread and at [the] festival of the weeks and at [the] festival of the booths.
pieces: making the offerings each day required, according to the commandment of Moses, on the Sabbaths, at the new moons, and at the appointed festivals three times a year: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths.

L.13: offering up as the matter of each day [required], according to the commandment of Moses, for the Sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed feasts three times in the year: at the festival of unleavened bread, and at the festival of weeks, and at the festival of booths.

R.13: He offered what was required for each day, as Moses had commanded. He offered sacrifices on the Sabbath days, at the New Moon feasts, and at the three festivals held each year: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths.

decisions.choice: the matter of a day in its day: what each day called for
decisions.reason: The phrase means the set requirement for each day, so the offerings followed the calendar day by day (compare 1 Chronicles 16:37).

decisions.choice: the commandment of Moses: the laws for daily and festival offerings
decisions.reason: The Law sets offerings for every day, for the Sabbaths and for the new moons (Numbers 28-29), and commands Israel to appear before the LORD at the three feasts (Exodus 23:14-17; Deuteronomy 16:16).

decisions.choice: new moons; the three feasts
decisions.reason: The new moon was the first day of each month. The three yearly feasts were Unleavened Bread in spring with Passover, Weeks at the wheat harvest, and Booths at the autumn harvest (Leviticus 23).

decisions.choice: Festival of Unleavened Bread, Festival of Weeks, Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the feasts as names, as in Deuteronomy 16:16, and Readable says "New Moon feasts" as in 1 Chronicles 23:31.

records.source: וַיַּעֲמֵ֣ד כְּמִשְׁפַּ֣ט דָּֽוִיד־אָ֠בִיו אֶת־מַחְלְק֨וֹת הַכֹּהֲנִ֜ים עַל־עֲבֹדָתָ֗ם וְהַלְוִיִּ֣ם עַל־מִ֠שְׁמְרוֹתָם לְהַלֵּ֨ל וּלְשָׁרֵ֜ת נֶ֤גֶד הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ לִדְבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֔וֹ וְהַשּׁוֹעֲרִ֥ים בְּמַחְלְקוֹתָ֖ם לְשַׁ֣עַר וָשָׁ֑עַר כִּ֣י כֵ֔ן מִצְוַ֖ת דָּוִ֥יד אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he appointed, according to [the] ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests over their service, and the Levites over their duties, to praise and to minister before the priests, as [the] matter of a day in its day, and the gatekeepers by their divisions for gate and gate; for so [was the] commandment of David the man of God.
pieces: Following the ordinance of his father David, he set the priests in their divisions over their service, and the Levites over their duties of praising and of ministering alongside the priests as each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate. For this was what David the man of God had commanded.

L.14: And he appointed, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties, to praise and to minister before the priests, as the matter of each day [required], and the gatekeepers by their divisions for each gate; for so [was] the commandment of David the man of God.

R.14: Solomon followed the rules his father David had made. He appointed the priests in their groups to do their work. He appointed the Levites to lead the praise and to help the priests with what had to be done each day. He also appointed the gatekeepers in their groups to guard each gate. This was what David, the man of God, had commanded.

decisions.choice: the ordinance of David: the arrangements of 1 Chronicles 23-26; no parallel in 1 Kings
decisions.reason: David divided the priests into twenty-four divisions (1 Chronicles 24), organized the Levites, singers and gatekeepers (chapters 23, 25-26), and gave Solomon the plan (1 Chronicles 28:13, 21). Here Solomon puts it into effect. 1 Kings has nothing of this.

decisions.choice: the man of God: a title usually given to prophets
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is used of Moses (Deuteronomy 33:1; 1 Chronicles 23:14) and of prophets. Giving it to David sets his commands for worship beside the commandment of Moses in verse 13, as Nehemiah 12:24, 36 also does.

decisions.choice: before the priests: in service to the priests
decisions.reason: The Levites assisted the priests and worked under them (1 Chronicles 23:28-32).

decisions.choice: alongside the priests
decisions.reason: Balanced says "alongside" for "before", since the Levites served beside and for the priests, not in front of them.

decisions.choice: lead the praise; help the priests; to guard each gate
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the Levites' praise and ministry were and what the gatekeepers did at each gate.

records.source: וְלֹ֣א סָרוּ֩ מִצְוַ֨ת הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ עַל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֛ם לְכָל־דָּבָ֖ר וְלָאֹצָרֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And not they turned aside [from the] commandment of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, and concerning the treasuries.
pieces: They did not depart from what the king had commanded the priests and the Levites in any matter, including the treasuries.

L.15: And they did not turn aside from the commandment of the king concerning the priests and the Levites in any matter, and concerning the treasuries.

R.15: No one turned away from what the king had commanded the priests and the Levites about anything, including the treasuries.

decisions.choice: the king: probably David, whose commandment verse 14 cites
decisions.reason: Verse 14 ends with "the commandment of David", so "the king" most likely means David. It may also mean Solomon, who put David's arrangements in place.

decisions.choice: concerning the priests and the Levites: the command about them, or to them
decisions.reason: "They" are the people bound by the king's command. The Hebrew can mean the command given to the priests and Levites, or the command about them; either way, it was kept in every detail.

decisions.choice: the treasuries: the temple storehouses
decisions.reason: Levites were put in charge of the temple treasuries and the gifts dedicated to the LORD (1 Chronicles 26:20-28).

decisions.choice: including
decisions.reason: The last phrase adds a particular case to "any matter"; Balanced and Readable mark it with "including".

records.source: וַתִּכֹּן֙ כָּל־מְלֶ֣אכֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַד־הַיּ֛וֹם מוּסַ֥ד בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וְעַד־כְּלֹת֑וֹ שָׁלֵ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And was established all [the] work of Solomon until the day of [the] foundation of [the] house of Yahweh and until its finishing; complete [was the] house of Yahweh.
pieces: So all Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was laid until it was finished. The house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was complete.

L.16: And all the work of Solomon was established, up to the day of the foundation of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and until it was finished; the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] complete.

R.16: All of Solomon's work was done, from the day the foundation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple was laid until the day it was finished. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple was complete.

decisions.choice: until the day of the foundation and until its finishing: from start to finish
alternatives: the work was prepared before the foundation was laid, and carried through to the end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "until the day of the foundation ... and until it was finished". It probably means that every stage of the work, up to the laying of the foundation and then up to the end, went as planned: the whole project, from beginning to end.

decisions.choice: was established: was prepared and carried through
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made firm, set in order or prepared (compare 1 Chronicles 22:14; 2 Chronicles 35:16).

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD was complete: compare 1 Kings 9:25
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:25 ends "and he completed the house" with a verb of the same root. Chronicles turns it into a closing statement: the temple was whole and finished.

decisions.choice: from the day the foundation ... was laid until
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable express the span with "from ... until", since "until the day of the foundation" in plain English would cut off the work before it started.

records.source: אָז֩ הָלַ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה לְעֶצְיֽוֹן־גֶּ֧בֶר וְאֶל־אֵיל֛וֹת עַל־שְׂפַ֥ת הַיָּ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אֱדֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: Then went Solomon to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on [the] shore of the sea in [the] land of Edom.
pieces: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the seacoast in the land of Edom.

L.17: Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the shore of the sea, in the land of Edom.

R.17: Then Solomon went to the towns of Ezion-geber and Eloth, on the coast of the Red Sea in the land of Edom.

decisions.choice: Solomon went to Ezion-geber; 1 Kings 9:26 says he made a fleet there
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 9:26 says that King Solomon made a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth, on the shore of the Sea of Reeds. Chronicles says that Solomon went there himself, calls it simply "the sea", and in verse 18 has Huram send the ships.

decisions.choice: Ezion-geber and Eloth: ports at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba
decisions.reason: Both lay at the northern tip of the eastern arm of the Red Sea, on the route Israel took in the wilderness (Numbers 33:35; Deuteronomy 2:8, where Eloth is spelled Elath). From there ships could sail south to Arabia and Africa.

decisions.choice: in the land of Edom: in territory under Solomon's control
decisions.reason: David had put garrisons in Edom (1 Chronicles 18:13), so this coast was in Israel's hands.

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: Readable names the sea, which 1 Kings 9:26 calls the Sea of Reeds, the Red Sea.

records.heading: Ships to Ophir

records.source: וַיִּֽשְׁלַֽח־לוֹ֩ חוּרָ֨ם בְּיַד־עֲבָדָ֜יו אֳנִיּ֗וֹת וַעֲבָדִים֮ י֣וֹדְעֵי יָם֒ וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עִם־עַבְדֵ֤י שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אוֹפִ֔ירָה וַיִּקְח֣וּ מִשָּׁ֔ם אַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֑ב וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶל־הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And sent to him Huram by [the] hand of his servants ships and servants knowing [the] sea, and they went with [the] servants of Solomon to Ophir, and they took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and brought [it] to the king Solomon.
pieces: Huram sent him ships under the command of his own servants, along with servants who knew the sea. They went with Solomon's servants to Ophir, and brought back from there {{units:about 33,750 pounds|450 talents}} of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon.

L.18: And Huram sent him, by the hand of his servants, ships and servants who knew the sea; and they went with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and took from there 450 talents of gold, and brought [it] to King Solomon.

R.18: Huram sent him ships, with his own men in charge and experienced sailors to crew them. They sailed to Ophir with Solomon's men and brought back {{units:about 33,750 pounds|450 talents}} of gold for King Solomon.

decisions.choice: Huram sent ships; 450 talents; 1 Kings 9:27-28 has Hiram send sailors and 420 talents
decisions.reason: In 1 Kings 9:27-28 Solomon built the fleet and Hiram sent experienced sailors to serve in it; they brought back 420 talents. Here Huram sends ships as well as men, and the gold weighs 450 talents. The figures may count the gold differently, or one may have changed in copying.

decisions.choice: by the hand of his servants: in the charge of his men
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" means through or under someone. How ships from Tyre on the Mediterranean reached the Red Sea is not said; they may have been built on the spot by Huram's men, or carried in parts overland.

decisions.choice: Ophir: a distant land famous for its gold
decisions.reason: Its location is not known; southern Arabia, the coast of East Africa and India have all been suggested. "Gold of Ophir" was a byword for the finest gold (Isaiah 13:12; Psalm 45:10; Job 28:16).

decisions.choice: talent: the largest weight, about 75 pounds
decisions.reason: A talent was 3,000 shekels. 450 talents of gold is about 33,750 pounds, nearly 17 tons.

decisions.choice: about 33,750 pounds (with 450 talents as the setting)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern weight, with the talent as the alternative, as in 1 Kings 9:28.

decisions.choice: experienced sailors; sailed; men
decisions.reason: Readable says "sailors" for servants who knew the sea, "sailed" since they went by ship, and "men" for each king's servants, as in 1 Kings 9:27-28.
